gloss: to pull in, to draw into

definitions.gloss: to pull in, to draw into
definitions.explanation: To bring or draw something or someone into a space or situation.
To get someone involved in a situation, often unwillingly.

examples.japanese: {客|きゃく}を{店|みせ}に{引|ひ}き{込|こ}む。
examples.english: To draw customers into the store.

examples.japanese: {物語|ものがたり}の{世界|せかい}に{引|ひ}き{込|こ}まれた。
examples.english: I was drawn into the world of the story.

examples.japanese: あの{映画|えいが}は{最初|さいしょ}の10{分|ぷん}で{観客|かんきゃく}を{引|ひ}き{込|こ}む{力|ちから}がある。
examples.english: That movie has the power to draw the audience in within the first ten minutes.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{話|はなし}し{方|かた}は{上手|じょうず}で、{聞|き}いている{人|ひと}を{自然|しぜん}と{引|ひ}き{込|こ}んでいく。
examples.english: He's a skilled speaker who naturally draws his listeners in.

examples.japanese: トラブルに{引|ひ}き{込|こ}まれた。
{友達|ともだち}を{喧嘩|けんか}に{引|ひ}き{込|こ}むな。
examples.english: Don't drag your friends into a fight.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{私|わたし}たちを{危険|きけん}な{計画|けいかく}に{引|ひ}き{込|こ}もうとした。
examples.english: He tried to drag us into a dangerous plan.

examples.japanese: {知|し}らない{間|あいだ}に{詐欺|さぎ}に{引|ひ}き{込|こ}まれていた。
examples.english: Before I knew it, I had been drawn into a scam.

examples.japanese: {関係|かんけい}のない{人|ひと}まで{問題|もんだい}に{引|ひ}き{込|こ}んでしまって、{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}なく{思|おも}っている。
examples.english: I feel sorry for having dragged even uninvolved people into the problem.

notes:
{引|ひ}き{込|こ}む is a compound verb meaning to pull/draw into. Transitive godan verb.

COMPOUND STRUCTURE:
{引|ひ}く (to pull) + {込|こ}む (into). The 〜{込|こ}む suffix adds the nuance of entering or going deeply into.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {客|きゃく}を{店|みせ}に{引|ひ}き{込|こ}む: to draw customers into a store
- {話|はなし}に{引|ひ}き{込|こ}まれる: to be drawn into a story
- トラブルに{引|ひ}き{込|こ}む: to drag into trouble

TRANSITIVITY:
- {引|ひ}き{込|こ}む ({他動詞|たどうし}): to pull in
- {引|ひ}きこもる ({自動詞|じどうし}): to shut oneself in, withdraw

RELATED:
{引|ひ}きこもり refers to social withdrawal or a person who stays isolated at home.
